corrections.text: The Sources and independence section says the independent accounts come from five outlets. Counted per outlet under the Herald's Analysis rules, the LWN.net piece is a contributed article by a guest author, and The New Stack's piece reports a program run by a vendor (Chainguard), so neither is counted as independent here. The outlets with their own reporting and no such label are InfoQ, It's FOSS and Linuxiac (three); only InfoQ and It's FOSS cover more than one of the four projects, and no outlet independent of HashiCorp covers Boundary, which rests on its README and the Herald's earlier briefing.

The closing paragraph says the three archived repositories carry three statements, including 'security patches only in the new image (LocalStack)'. That wording is InfoQ's account of LocalStack's February 2026 announcement ('with product enhancements and security patches applied only to the new version'); the LocalStack repository's README, dated 2026-03-23, does not state a security-fix position, and the Herald did not read the announcement itself.
